verses.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַֽחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת שָׁא֔וּל וְדָוִ֣ד שָׁ֔ב מֵהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־ הָעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב דָּוִ֛ד בְּצִקְלָ֖ג יָמִ֥ים שְׁנָֽיִם׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ’a·ḥă·rê mō·wṯ šā·’ūl wə·ḏā·wiḏ šāḇ mê·hak·kō·wṯ ’eṯ- hā·‘ă·mā·lêq way·yê·šeḇ dā·wiḏ bə·ṣiq·lāḡ yā·mîm šə·nā·yim
verses.literal: After the death of Saul David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed . . . in Ziklag two days
verses.literalPt: E SUCEDEU que, depois da morte de Saul, voltando Davi da derrota dos amalequitas, ficou dois dias em Ziclague;

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וְהִנֵּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ בָּ֤א מִן־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וּבְגָדָ֣יו קְרֻעִ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיְהִי֙ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî bay·yō·wm haš·šə·lî·šî wə·hin·nêh ’îš bā min- ham·ma·ḥă·neh mê·‘im šā·’ūl ū·ḇə·ḡā·ḏāw qə·ru·‘îm wa·’ă·ḏā·māh ‘al- rō·šōw way·hî bə·ḇō·’ōw ’el- dā·wiḏ way·yip·pōl ’ar·ṣāh way·yiš·tā·ḥū
verses.literal: On the third . . . day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp . . . When he came to David he fell to the ground to pay him homage
verses.literalPt: Ao terceiro dia um homem veio do arraial de Saul, com as vestes rotas e com terra sobre a cabeça; e, chegando ele a Davi, se lançou no chão, e se inclinou.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּב֑וֹא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו מִמַּחֲנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִמְלָֽטְתִּי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lōw dā·wiḏ ’ê miz·zeh tā·ḇō·w way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw mim·ma·ḥă·nêh yiś·rā·’êl nim·lā·ṭə·tî
verses.literal: Where . . . have you come from David asked I have escaped from the Israelite camp he replied
verses.literalPt: E Davi lhe disse: Donde vens? E ele lhe disse: Escapei do arraial de Israel.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו דָּוִ֛ד מֶה־ הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַגֶּד־ נָ֣א לִ֑י וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֲשֶׁר־ נָ֨ס הָעָ֜ם מִן־ הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְגַם־ הַרְבֵּ֞ה נָפַ֤ל מִן־ הָעָם֙ וַיָּמֻ֔תוּ וְגַ֗ם שָׁא֛וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ מֵֽתוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw dā·wiḏ meh- hā·yāh had·dā·ḇār hag·geḏ- nā lî way·yō·mer ’ă·šer- nās hā·‘ām min- ham·mil·ḥā·māh wə·ḡam- har·bêh nā·p̄al min- hā·‘ām way·yā·mu·ṯū wə·ḡam šā·’ūl wî·hō·w·nā·ṯān bə·nōw mê·ṯū
verses.literal: What was the outcome . . . David asked . . . Please tell me The troops fled from the battle he replied - Many of them fell and died And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhe Davi: Como foi lá isso? peço-te, dize-mo. E ele lhe respondeu: O povo fugiu da batalha, e muitos do povo caíram, e morreram; assim como também Saul e Jônatas, seu filho, foram mortos.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד אֶל־ הַנַּ֖עַר הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֑וֹ אֵ֣יךְ יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי־ מֵ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל וִיהֽוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ ’el- han·na·‘ar ham·mag·gîḏ lōw ’êḵ yā·ḏa‘·tā kî- mêṯ šā·’ūl wî·hō·w·nā·ṯān bə·nōw
verses.literal: Then David . . . asked the young man who had brought him the report . . . How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead
verses.literalPt: E disse Davi ao moço que lhe trazia as novas: Como sabes tu que Saul e Jônatas, seu filho, foram mortos?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הַנַּ֣עַר׀ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֗וֹ נִקְרֹ֤א נִקְרֵ֙יתִי֙ בְּהַ֣ר הַגִּלְבֹּ֔עַ וְהִנֵּ֥ה שָׁא֖וּל נִשְׁעָ֣ן עַל־ חֲנִית֑וֹ וְהִנֵּ֥ה הָרֶ֛כֶב וּבַעֲלֵ֥י הַפָּרָשִׁ֖ים הִדְבִּקֻֽהוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer han·na·‘ar ham·mag·gîḏ lōw niq·rō niq·rê·ṯî bə·har hag·gil·bō·a‘ wə·hin·nêh šā·’ūl niš·‘ān ‘al- ḥă·nî·ṯōw wə·hin·nêh hā·re·ḵeḇ ū·ḇa·‘ă·lê hap·pā·rā·šîm hiḏ·bi·qu·hū
verses.literal: I happened . . . to be on Mount Gilboa he - replied and there was Saul leaning on his spear with the chariots . . . and the cavalry closing in on him
verses.literalPt: Então disse o moço que lhe dava a notícia: Cheguei por acaso à montanha de Gilboa, e eis que Saul estava encostado sobre a sua lança, e eis que os carros e a cavalaria apertavam-no.

verses.original: וַיִּ֥פֶן אַחֲרָ֖יו וַיִּרְאֵ֑נִי וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֵלָ֔י וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yi·p̄en ’a·ḥă·rāw way·yir·’ê·nî way·yiq·rā ’ê·lāy wā·’ō·mar hin·nê·nî
verses.literal: When he turned around . . . and saw me he called out to me and I answered Here I am
verses.literalPt: E, olhando ele para trás de si, viu-me, e chamou-me; e eu disse: Eis-me aqui.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֖י מִי־ אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָ֔יו עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lî mî- ’āt·tāh way·yō·mɛr ’ê·lāw ‘ă·mā·lê·qî ’ā·nō·ḵî
verses.literal: Who are you he asked So I told him I am an Amalekite
verses.literalPt: E ele me disse: Quem és tu? E eu lhe disse: Sou amalequita.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י עֲמָד־ נָ֤א עָלַי֙ וּמֹ֣תְתֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֲחָזַ֖נִי הַשָּׁבָ֑ץ כִּֽי־ כָל־ ע֥וֹד נַפְשִׁ֖י בִּֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ê·lay ‘ă·māḏ- nā ‘ā·lay ū·mō·ṯə·ṯê·nî kî ’ă·ḥā·za·nî haš·šā·ḇāṣ kî- ḵāl ‘ō·wḏ nap̄·šî bî
verses.literal: Then he begged me . . . Stand . . . over me and kill me for agony has seized me but my life . . . still lingers
verses.literalPt: Então ele me disse: Peço-te, arremessa-te sobre mim, e mata-me, porque angústias me têm cercado, pois toda a minha vida está ainda em mim.

verses.original: וָאֶעֱמֹ֤ד עָלָיו֙ וַאֲמֹ֣תְתֵ֔הוּ כִּ֣י יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽחְיֶ֖ה אַחֲרֵ֣י נִפְל֑וֹ וָאֶקַּ֞ח הַנֵּ֣זֶר׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ רֹאשׁ֗וֹ וְאֶצְעָדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ זְרֹע֔וֹ וָאֲבִיאֵ֥ם אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הֵֽנָּה׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’e·‘ĕ·mōḏ ‘ā·lāw wa·’ă·mō·ṯə·ṯê·hū kî yā·ḏa‘·tî kî lō yiḥ·yeh ’a·ḥă·rê nip̄·lōw wā·’eq·qaḥ han·nê·zer ’ă·šer ‘al- rō·šōw wə·’eṣ·‘ā·ḏāh ’ă·šer ‘al- zə·rō·‘ōw wā·’ă·ḇî·’êm ’el- ’ă·ḏō·nî hên·nāh
verses.literal: So I stood over him and killed him because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm and I have brought them here to my lord
verses.literalPt: Arremessei-me, pois, sobre ele, e o matei, porque bem sabia eu que não viveria depois da sua queda, e tomei a coroa que tinha na cabeça, e o bracelete que trazia no braço, e os trouxe aqui a meu senhor.

verses.original: וַיַּחֲזֵ֥ק דָּוִ֛ד בִּבְגָדוֹ וַיִּקְרָעֵ֑ם וְגַ֥ם כָּל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·ḥă·zêq dā·wiḏ biḇ·ḡå̄·ḏō way·yiq·rā·‘êm wə·ḡam kāl- hā·’ă·nā·šîm ’ă·šer ’it·tōw
verses.literal: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them and all the men who were with him did the same
verses.literalPt: Então apanhou Davi as suas vestes, e as rasgou; assim fizeram todos os homens que estavam com ele.

verses.original: וַֽיִּסְפְּדוּ֙ וַיִּבְכּ֔וּ וַיָּצֻ֖מוּ עַד־ הָעָ֑רֶב עַל־ שָׁא֞וּל וְעַל־ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֗וֹ וְעַל־ עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ וְעַל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י נָפְל֖וּ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yis·pə·ḏū way·yiḇ·kū way·yā·ṣu·mū ‘aḏ- hā·‘ā·reḇ ‘al- šā·’ūl wə·‘al- yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān bə·nōw wə·‘al- ‘am Yah·weh wə·‘al- bêṯ yiś·rā·’êl kî nā·p̄ə·lū be·ḥā·reḇ
verses.literal: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son . . . Jonathan and for the people of the LORD . . . and the house of Israel because they had fallen by the sword
verses.literalPt: E prantearam, e choraram, e jejuaram até à tarde por Saul, e por Jônatas, seu filho, e pelo povo do SENHOR, e pela casa de Israel, porque tinham caído à espada.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל־ הַנַּ֙עַר֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בֶּן־ אִ֛ישׁ גֵּ֥ר עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ ’el- han·na·‘ar ham·mag·gîḏ lōw ’ê miz·zeh ’āt·tāh way·yō·mer ben- ’îš gêr ‘ă·mā·lê·qî ’ā·nō·ḵî
verses.literal: And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report . . . Where . . . are you from I am the son . . . of a foreigner he answered I am an Amalekite
verses.literalPt: Disse então Davi ao moço que lhe trouxera a nova: Donde és tu? E disse ele: Sou filho de um estrangeiro, amalequita.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דָּוִ֑ד אֵ֚יךְ לֹ֣א יָרֵ֔אתָ לִשְׁלֹ֙חַ֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ לְשַׁחֵ֖ת אֶת־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw dā·wiḏ ’êḵ lō yā·rê·ṯā liš·lō·aḥ yā·ḏə·ḵā lə·ša·ḥêṯ ’eṯ- mə·šî·aḥ Yah·weh
verses.literal: So David asked him Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed
verses.literalPt: E Davi lhe disse: Como não temeste tu estender a mão para matares ao ungido do SENHOR?

verses.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א דָוִ֗ד לְאַחַד֙ מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֔ים וַיֹּ֖אמֶר גַּ֣שׁ פְּגַע־ בּ֑וֹ וַיַּכֵּ֖הוּ וַיָּמֹֽת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·rā ḏā·wiḏ lə·’a·ḥaḏ mê·han·nə·‘ā·rîm way·yō·mer gaš pə·ḡa‘- bōw way·yak·kê·hū way·yā·mōṯ
verses.literal: Then David summoned one of the young men and said Go execute him So the young man struck him down and he died
verses.literalPt: Então chamou Davi a um dos moços, e disse: Chega, e lança-te sobre ele. E ele o feriu, e morreu.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ דָּוִ֔ד דָּמֶיךָ עַל־ רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֣י פִ֗יךָ עָנָ֤ה בְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָנֹכִ֥י מֹתַ֖תִּי אֶת־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw dā·wiḏ då̄·mɛ·ḵå̄ ‘al- rō·še·ḵā kî p̄î·ḵā ‘ā·nāh ḇə·ḵā lê·mōr ’ā·nō·ḵî mō·ṯat·tî ’eṯ- mə·šî·aḥ Yah·weh
verses.literal: For David had said to the Amalekite Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you saying I killed the LORD’s anointed
verses.literalPt: Pois Davi lhe dissera: O teu sangue seja sobre a tua cabeça, porque a tua própria boca testificou contra ti, dizendo: Eu matei o ungido do SENHOR.

verses.original: וַיְקֹנֵ֣ן דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־ הַקִּינָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את עַל־ שָׁא֖וּל וְעַל־ יְהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·qō·nên dā·wiḏ ’eṯ- haq·qî·nāh haz·zōṯ ‘al- šā·’ūl wə·‘al- yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān bə·nōw
verses.literal: Then David took up this lament for Saul . . . and his son Jonathan
verses.literalPt: E lamentou Davi a Saul e a Jônatas, seu filho, com esta lamentação

verses.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְלַמֵּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֖ה קָ֑שֶׁת הִנֵּ֥ה כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל־ סֵ֥פֶר הַיָּשָֽׁר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lə·lam·mêḏ bə·nê- yə·hū·ḏāh qā·šeṯ hin·nêh ḵə·ṯū·ḇāh ‘al- sê·p̄er hay·yā·šār
verses.literal: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow . . . It is written in the Book of Jashar
verses.literalPt: (Dizendo ele que ensinassem aos filhos de Judá o uso do arco. Eis que está escrito no livro de Jasher):

verses.original: הַצְּבִי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַל־ בָּמוֹתֶ֖יךָ חָלָ֑ל אֵ֖יךְ נָפְל֥וּ גִבּוֹרִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: haṣ·ṣə·ḇî yiś·rā·’êl ‘al- bā·mō·w·ṯe·ḵā ḥā·lāl ’êḵ nā·p̄ə·lū ḡib·bō·w·rîm
verses.literal: Your glory O Israel lies slain on your heights How the mighty have fallen
verses.literalPt: Ah, ornamento de Israel! Nos teus altos foi ferido, como caíram os poderosos!

verses.original: אַל־ תַּגִּ֣ידוּ בְגַ֔ת אַֽל־ תְּבַשְּׂר֖וּ בְּחוּצֹ֣ת אַשְׁקְל֑וֹן פֶּן־ תִּשְׂמַ֙חְנָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים פֶּֽן־ תַּעֲלֹ֖זְנָה בְּנ֥וֹת הָעֲרֵלִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: ’al- tag·gî·ḏū ḇə·ḡaṯ ’al- tə·ḇaś·śə·rū bə·ḥū·ṣōṯ ’aš·qə·lō·wn pen- tiś·maḥ·nāh bə·nō·wṯ pə·liš·tîm pen- ta·‘ă·lō·zə·nāh bə·nō·wṯ hā·‘ă·rê·lîm
verses.literal: Tell it not in Gath proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon lest the daughters of the Philistines . . . rejoice and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult
verses.literalPt: Não o noticieis em Gate, não o publiqueis nas ruas de Ascalom, para que não se alegrem as filhas dos filisteus, para que não saltem de contentamento as filhas dos incircuncisos.

verses.original: הָרֵ֣י בַגִּלְבֹּ֗עַ אַל־ טַ֧ל וְאַל־ מָטָ֛ר עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם וּשְׂדֵ֣י תְרוּמֹ֑ת כִּ֣י שָׁ֤ם נִגְעַל֙ מָגֵ֣ן גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים מָגֵ֣ן שָׁא֔וּל בְּלִ֖י מָשִׁ֥יחַ בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃
verses.transliteration: hā·rê ḇag·gil·bō·a‘ ’al- ṭal wə·’al- mā·ṭār ‘ă·lê·ḵem ū·śə·ḏê ṯə·rū·mōṯ kî šām niḡ·‘al mā·ḡên gib·bō·w·rîm mā·ḡên šā·’ūl bə·lî mā·šî·aḥ baš·šā·men
verses.literal: O mountains of Gilboa may you have no dew . . . or rain no fields yielding offerings of grain For there the shield of the mighty was defiled the shield of Saul no longer anointed with oil
verses.literalPt: Vós, montes de Gilboa, nem orvalho, nem chuva caia sobre vós, nem haja campos de ofertas alçadas, pois aí desprezivelmente foi arrojado o escudo dos poderosos, o escudo de Saul, como se não fora ungido com óleo.

verses.original: מִדַּ֣ם חֲלָלִ֗ים מֵחֵ֙לֶב֙ גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים קֶ֚שֶׁת יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן לֹ֥א נָשׂ֖וֹג אָח֑וֹר וְחֶ֣רֶב שָׁא֔וּל לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב רֵיקָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: mid·dam ḥă·lā·lîm mê·ḥê·leḇ gib·bō·w·rîm qe·šeṯ yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān lō nā·śō·wḡ ’ā·ḥō·wr wə·ḥe·reḇ šā·’ūl lō ṯā·šūḇ rê·qām
verses.literal: From the blood of the slain from the fat of the mighty the bow of Jonathan did not retreat . . . and the sword of Saul did not return empty
verses.literalPt: Do sangue dos feridos, da gordura dos valentes, nunca se retirou para trás o arco de Jônatas, nem voltou vazia a espada de Saul.

verses.original: שָׁא֣וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֗ן הַנֶּאֱהָבִ֤ים וְהַנְּעִימִם֙ בְּחַיֵּיהֶ֔ם וּבְמוֹתָ֖ם לֹ֣א נִפְרָ֑דוּ מִנְּשָׁרִ֣ים קַ֔לּוּ מֵאֲרָי֖וֹת גָּבֵֽרוּ׃
verses.transliteration: šā·’ūl wî·hō·w·nā·ṯān han·ne·’ĕ·hā·ḇîm wə·han·nə·‘î·mim bə·ḥay·yê·hem ū·ḇə·mō·w·ṯām lō nip̄·rā·ḏū min·nə·šā·rîm qal·lū mê·’ă·rā·yō·wṯ gā·ḇê·rū
verses.literal: Saul and Jonathan beloved and delightful in life were not divided in death They were swifter than eagles they were stronger than lions
verses.literalPt: Saul e Jônatas, tão amados e queridos na sua vida, também na sua morte não se separaram; eram mais ligeiros do que as águias, mais fortes do que os leões.

verses.original: בְּנוֹת֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־ שָׁא֖וּל בְּכֶ֑ינָה הַמַּלְבִּֽשְׁכֶ֤ם שָׁנִי֙ עִם־ עֲדָנִ֔ים הַֽמַּעֲלֶה֙ עֲדִ֣י זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל לְבוּשְׁכֶֽן׃
verses.transliteration: bə·nō·wṯ yiś·rā·’êl ’el- šā·’ūl bə·ḵe·nāh ham·mal·biš·ḵem šā·nî ‘im- ‘ă·ḏā·nîm ham·ma·‘ă·leh ‘ă·ḏî zā·hāḇ ‘al lə·ḇū·šə·ḵen
verses.literal: O daughters of Israel weep for Saul who clothed you in scarlet and luxury who decked your garments with ornaments of gold
verses.literalPt: Vós, filhas de Israel, chorai por Saul, que vos vestia de escarlata em delícias, que vos fazia trazer ornamentos de ouro sobre as vossas vestes.

verses.original: אֵ֚יךְ נָפְל֣וּ גִבֹּרִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן עַל־ בָּמוֹתֶ֖יךָ חָלָֽל׃
verses.transliteration: ’êḵ nā·p̄ə·lū ḡib·bō·rîm bə·ṯō·wḵ ham·mil·ḥā·māh yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān ‘al- bā·mō·w·ṯe·ḵā ḥā·lāl
verses.literal: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle Jonathan lies slain on your heights
verses.literalPt: Como caíram os poderosos, no meio da peleja! Jônatas nos teus altos foi morto.

verses.original: צַר־ לִ֣י עָלֶ֗יךָ אָחִי֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן נָעַ֥מְתָּ לִּ֖י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְלְאַ֤תָה אַהֲבָֽתְךָ֙ לִ֔י מֵאַהֲבַ֖ת נָשִֽׁים׃
verses.transliteration: ṣar- lî ‘ā·le·ḵā ’ā·ḥî yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān nā·‘am·tā lî mə·’ōḏ nip̄·lə·’a·ṯāh ’a·hă·ḇā·ṯə·ḵā lî mê·’a·hă·ḇaṯ nā·šîm
verses.literal: I grieve . . . for you Jonathan my brother You were delightful to me . . . your love to me was extraordinary surpassing the love of women
verses.literalPt: Angustiado estou por ti, meu irmão Jônatas; quão amabilíssimo me eras! Mais maravilhoso me era o teu amor do que o amor das mulheres.

verses.original: אֵ֚יךְ נָפְל֣וּ גִבּוֹרִ֔ים וַיֹּאבְד֖וּ כְּלֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה׃פ
verses.transliteration: ’êḵ nā·p̄ə·lū ḡib·bō·w·rîm way·yō·ḇə·ḏū kə·lê mil·ḥā·māh
verses.literal: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished
verses.literalPt: Como caíram os poderosos, e pereceram as armas de guerra!
